title: Structure and Determinants of Financial Covenants in Leveraged Buyouts

rival_explanations: the competing increased financial risk argument (covenant restrictiveness driven by leverage/financial risk rather than reduced information asymmetry costs)
reverse causality / simultaneous causality (endogeneity) between leverage and covenant restrictiveness, addressed with Wu–Hausman/instrumental-variable tests
agency-theory underinvestment account in which high-growth firms receive more restrictive covenants (Billett, King, and Mauer, 2007)

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (German leveraged buyouts across sectors; industry controlled via fixed effects / two-digit SIC matching)
context.country_region: Germany (LBO sample); nonsponsored benchmark from DealScan conditioned on Compustat data
context.sample_description: Proprietary LBO loan contracts and financial information negotiated between banks and PE sponsors, collected from three major European commercial banks (as lead/co-lead arrangers); benchmark samples of nonsponsored loans (term loans; and loans for corporate acquisitions) from Reuters LPC DealScan, conditioned on availability of Compustat data for the borrower
context.sample_size: 130 PE-sponsored LBO deals (126 observations in the D/EBITDA headroom regression); benchmark = 1,423 nonsponsored term-loan observations

data_sources.name: Proprietary LBO data set from three major European commercial banks (complete underwritten senior and subordinated loan contracts, original syndication memorandum, and underlying financial models)

analyses.label: Table IV: Frequency of financial covenants (sponsored vs nonsponsored loans)
analyses.sample: 130 PE-sponsored loans vs 1,423 nonsponsored term loans (and 355 highest D/EV quartile), 2000-2008

dv.name: Inclusion / number of financial covenants
dv.measure: inclusion of financial covenants (D/EBITDA, EBITDA/I, cash flow coverage, capex, D/E, current ratio, net worth) and 'No. of financial covenants' per loan deal
dv.source: Proprietary LBO data set from three banks (sponsored loans); Reuters LPC DealScan (nonsponsored loans)
